title: slimline-build-image-and-cached-dep-refresh
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: reduce CI image size and presubmit latency while improving dependency refresh hygiene. This PR introduces a slim build image for the majority of Lint/Test lanes, a small cache-warming helper that prefetches common dependency layers, and an automated weekly dep-refresh job that updates pinned devdeps and raises PRs for non-breaking upgrades. Key goals: 1) shorten cold CI worker startup and container pull times; 2) reduce transient network-induced flakiness by warming the remote cache for the most common toolchains; 3) keep dev dependency drift under control with an opt-in auto-PR flow. Changes are designed to be additive and guarded under a feature flag (CI_SLIM_BUILD=true) so rollout can be staged. See the checklist below and the related Linear cards.

Checklist: - [x] add slim Dockerfile and publish manifest to the internal registry - [x] implement cache-warm helper script with idempotent semantics - [x] wire slim image into GH Actions build matrix behind CI_SLIM_BUILD flag - [x] add weekly dep-refresh workflow and depbot fallback - [x] update docs: CONTRIBUTING.md and CI-runbook - [x] smoke test on staging runner and monitor DB of flakes for 72h

Context and links: Linear ENG-1728 (CI performance audit), ENG-1734 (dep hygiene initiative). Related infra doc: https://internal.redwood.ai/docs/ci-cache-strategy. This PR intentionally avoids changing production runtime images or release artifacts; it focuses on developer/CI ergonomics.
commits: c3f5a7b: add Dockerfile.slim and build manifest + CI publish step
1a2b3f4: implement scripts/cache-warm.sh with retries and ttl
review_comments: Aaron Patel: Nice direction. A couple questions: is the slim image missing any platform-specific deps needed for Linux-musl runners? Please add a short matrix in build.yml to validate musl vs glibc images.
Maya Chen: The slim image is intentionally glibc-based for now. I added a small validation job in build.yml and a TODO to extend to musl once we confirm libc compatibility across our toolchains.
Lina Gomez: cache-warm looks good but please make the helper tolerant to 429s and add exponential backoff. Also make TTL configurable via env var.
Maya Chen: Updated cache-warm to respect CACHE_WARM_TTL and added exponential backoff (up to 6 retries). Tests added to tools/dep-refresh/README.md to document behavior.
Tomoko Saito: The weekly dep-refresh job should not auto-merge. Can we gate auto-PRs behind a label and add an owner-review bot?
Maya Chen: Agreed. The job now opens a draft PR and tags it with 'dep-refresh'. We added a rule in the repo settings for human approval; auto-merge is disabled by default.
